item.title: codex security
item.description:
The Problem
Code repositories accumulate security vulnerabilities that are easy to miss in manual review and hard to track across branches or over time. Existing scanners often produce noise, lack CI integration, or require separate tooling for triage, remediation, and policy enforcement. Teams need a single pipeline that finds, validates, and fixes issues without switching contexts.

item.title: see through walls
item.description:
The Problem Real-time multiplayer AR typically breaks down when participants move behind physical obstacles—walls block line-of-sight, breaking spatial awareness. Existing solutions either require expensive infrastructure or fail to maintain a shared reference frame across devices. This repo demonstrates a practical fix using MultiSet’s Visual Positioning System (VPS) to align all devices to the same 3D map, then render avatars behind walls as glowing skeletons.

item.title: googlemaps scraper
item.description:
The Problem
Extracting structured business data from Google Maps at scale is unreliable and labor-intensive. Manual copy-paste yields a few dozen records; existing scrapers often break, limit results per query, or charge per lead. Teams need a tool that returns thousands of usable leads—including emails and social profiles—without recurring API fees.

item.title: asm
item.description:

Installing the same skill across multiple tools means manual copying, version drift, and no way to audit what’s actually active. Teams waste time chasing outdated or duplicate skill files across hidden folders.

item.title: buzz
item.description:
The Problem
Most AI-adjacent collaboration tools treat agents as second-class citizens — bolted-on chatbots with limited permissions, no audit trail, and no ability to act on the workspace itself. Teams end up with fragmented identity models (one for people, one for bots) and no unified record of who did what, whether human or agent.

item.title: MoonEP
item.description:
The Problem
Expert parallelism (EP) in Mixture-of-Experts models is fundamentally unbalanced: router output skews token loads across ranks, so some ranks receive far more than S × K tokens. This drives up iteration time (the hottest rank sets the pace) and fragments GPU memory until training OOMs. Existing libraries like DeepEP v2 suffer from both problems.
